messages:
maya: Heads-up — onboarding nova-7b-q4 variant to the eval harness CI is failing for some chat-config cases. Seeing a big drop in response_consistency after quantized runs, but float runs are fine. attaching logs and quick notes :grimacing:

jon: what are the numbers? spike where?

maya: baseline ~0.92 -> quantized ~0.74 on daily regression suite (convo-style bench). Not a perf regress, seems like metric instability. The CI job shows model/tokenizer mismatch warnings in the log but no hard fail.

samir: which tokenizer are we using in the harness for this model? HF or the model-provided qtk?

maya: harness catalog picked `auto` -> ended up using the quant artifact's tokenizer (qtk). I ran a local tokenize dump and noticed the system prompt sentinel is split differently between hf and qtk. Paste of the chat template: ```role:system
content: "<SYS> You are a helpful assistant."
role:user
content: "Tell me the plan."```

liz: that looks like the classic prefix-sentinel boundary bug — our collate step can trim leading whitespace in the system role which moves token boundaries. we saw that before with whitespace-normalized templates.

jon: do you have the CI job id? can we repro locally with the exact artifact and config?

maya: ci/board-1887. repro command I used: ```./tools/eval_runner --model nova-7b-q4 --artifact quant --suite convo-daily --collate-config=chat --keep-sentinels=false```
The collate snippet in the runner that might be suspicious: ```python
# collate.py
def collate_chat(parts):
    # naive trim to avoid leading/trailing blanks
    for p in parts:
        p['content'] = p['content'].strip()
    return join_parts(parts)
```
That `strip()` is likely shifting the sentinel when tokenizer encodes differently.

samir: quick test suggestion: run with `--keep-sentinels=true` and compare token offsets: `python -m tokenizer.debug --model-path /tmp/artifact --show-offsets`. If qtk tokenizes `<SYS>` into two tokens while hf keeps it as one, downstream normalized-string metrics will diverge.

maya: ran that. Output shows `<SYS>` -> [`<`, `SYS`, `>`] under qtk vs [`<SYS>`] under hf. So quant tokenizer mapping differs — likely a conversion step in the quant build.

liz: so two mitigations: 1) override catalog to force `tokenizer: hf` for the quant artifact (stop auto pick), 2) make the metric `response_consistency` robust to tokenization by comparing normalized whitespace/Unicode and using sentence-level normalization instead of token offsets. Also we should avoid `strip()` when role==system or keep an explicit sentinel-preserve flag.

jon: please open two follow-ups: one small PR to set tokenizer override and a runner change to log the tokenizer name at job start, another GH issue to rework the metric to be tokenizer-agnostic. I can take the metric GH.

maya: will do. Drafted quick PR in fork to set `tokenizer: hf` in eval-catalog for nova-7b-q4 and add a unit test: `tests/test_tokenizer_consistency.py` that loads both artifacts and asserts `tokenizer.encode(system_prompt)` yields same token sequence. Also adding runner log: `logger.info(f"tokenizer={tokenizer.name} artifact_tokenizer={artifact.tokenizer}")`.

samir: +1. Also add a CI check that warns (and fails opt-in) if tokenizer names differ between artifact and catalog.

ci-bot: CI started for maya/nova-tokenizer-fix PR #8912 — status: running :gear:

maya: thanks — I'll post results here. If green we can roll the catalog change and re-run the daily suite. :crossed_fingers:
